jobs.occupation: PhD epidemiology of kidney replacement therapy in Europe
jobs.description: We are looking for an enthusiastic PhD _tudent to perform epidemiological research on patients treated by dialysis or kidney transplantation in an international environment. You will conduct epidemiological research on patients receiving kidney replacement therapy across European countries, investigating its occurrence, patient characteristics, and clinical outcomes. By expanding our database with newly available variables, you will address important knowledge gaps and explore new research questions in the fields of dialysis and kidney transplantation. You will analyze data and publish your findings in scientific papers that will form the basis of your PhD thesis. By identifying differences between countries, your research may contribute to a better understanding of kidney care across Europe and support country-specific healthcare planning and prioritization. Would you like to know more about the different phases within the PhD trajectory? You can read more about this on this page. You will conduct epidemiological research on patients with kidney disease across European countries, primarily utilizing data from the European Renal Association (ERA) Registry. This is a large European registry that collects data on patients with kidney failure undergoing dialysis or kidney transplantation from around 35 countries across Europe. In addition to your research, you will contribute to the annual data collection of the ERA Registry, and will assist in the publication of the ERA Registry’s annual report and related scientific articles. Currently the team consists of several senior/postdoctoral researchers, three PhD _tudents, a data manager and a management assistant who work intensively together and with nephrologists from different European countries. Throughout your PhD project, you will have the opportunity to fosteryour professional growth by participating in various courses, including those in epidemiology and scientific writing. an MSc degree in the field ofepidemiology, medicine, pharmacy, nutrition, medical informatics or (biomedical) health science; a strong motivation to pursue a PhD in epidemiological research; enthusiasm to participate in data collection processes; a service-oriented approach to communicating with international partners; proficiency in English, with strong written and oral communication skills; a detail-oriented approach to ensure high data quality and scientific accuracy. Applicants must hold a Master’s degree that is recognised and valid in the Netherlands. It is the applicant’s own responsibility to verify that their degree meets this requirement before applying. We are unable to assess or confirm the validity or recognition of individual diplomas by email. You will be employed by Amsterdam UMC Research BV. A contract for 12 months, with the intention to extend for a total of four years. The Guideline PhD contract applies to this vacancy. Classification in salary scale OIO: € 3.217 to € 4.077 gross for full-time employment (depending on experience). In addition to a good basic salary, we offer 8.3% end-of-year bonus. Medical doctors that are BIG-registered in the Netherlands are classified in salary scale 10: € 3.724 to € 5.867 gross for full-time employment (depending on experience). Calculate your net salary here. Holiday hours: 194.4 per year for full time and a possibility to save additional hours. 100% reimbursement for public transport travel costs. If you travel by foot, bicycle, or car, a mileage allowance of €0.21 per km applies (up to a maximum of 40 km one way by car). Do you prefer walking or cycling? Take advantage of our good bike scheme. Pension accrual with BeFrank, a modern, comprehensible and fairly priced pension. Watch this video with more information about joining Amsterdam UMC Research BV.
